translationRepairs: Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang—a maternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.
Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang—a younger paternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.
從父弟 is younger paternal cousin (father’s brother’s son); maternal cousin misreads 從父 as maternal line.
Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang, a younger cousin on his mother's side of Empress Wenxian.
Zhang Hongce, styled Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang, a younger paternal cousin of Empress Wenxian.
從父弟 marks paternal-line cousinage; “on his mother’s side” invents a maternal reading absent from 從父.
At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Yun to comfort the armies.
At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Guai to comfort the armies.
宗夬 is Zong Guai (夬 guài); Yun would require 雲 and is a wrong reading of the given name.
At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Yun to comfort the armies.
At Yangkou, Emperor He sent imperial censor Zong Guai to comfort the armies.
Same name error on the literal field: 宗夬 is Guai, not Yun.
Yu pressed Yun: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."
Yu pressed Guai: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."
域乃諷夬曰 addresses 夬 (Guai); continuing Yun repeats the 宗夬 misreading.
Yu pressed Yun: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."
Yu pressed Guai: "Without the yellow battle-ax you cannot command the lords."
Literal likewise must render 夬 as Guai, the same person as 宗夬 in s0080.
Yun went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.
Guai went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.
夬反西臺 continues 宗夬; subject is Guai returning west, not Yun.
Yun went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.
Guai went back to the western headquarters, and the yellow battle-ax was given to Gaozu at once.
Literal must match: 夬 is Guai’s given name, carried from 宗夬.
Inspector Xiao Yan's younger brother Shen had been put to death; when court troops came to take Yan, his attendants fled in panic, but Shaoshu alone rode to him at the news.
Inspector Xiao Dan's younger brother Shen had been put to death; when court troops came to take Dan, his attendants fled in panic, but Shaoshu alone rode to him at the news.
刺史蕭誕 is Xiao Dan (誕); Yan confuses him with Gaozu’s personal name 衍, and s0101 already has Dan.

When the righteous army rose, he became General of the Champions, then General of Valiant Cavalry, and marched east to Jiangzhou; Shaoshu stayed to govern the province and supply Jiang and Xiang with grain, without a single lapse.

When the righteous army rose, Shaoshu was made General of the Champions, then General of Valiant Cavalry; accompanying the eastern advance to Jiangzhou, he was left to oversee the province and supervise grain transport for Jiang and Xiang, without a single lapse.
Unstated 爲冠軍將軍…侍從東下江州 is Shaoshu; 留紹叔監州事 then leaves him to oversee—original splits one actor into two.

Posthumously: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with martial music, Eastern Garden rites, court robes, a full suit, and whatever the funeral demands supplied at need.

Posthumously: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards, with one set of martial music, Eastern Garden burial vessels, one court robe, one suit of garments, and whatever the funeral required supplied as needed.
東園秘器 are Eastern Garden burial vessels/coffins, not rites; 鼓吹一部/朝服一具/衣一襲 also support the counted wording.
諡曰忠 is a posthumous name (諡); temple name would be 廟號.
Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen begged to go west and was made Magistrate of Zou.
Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen begged to go west and was made Magistrate of Qi.
邔令 is magistrate of Qi (邔 Qǐ); Zou misreads a different place name.
By then Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen pressed hard to return west and was appointed Magistrate of Zou.
By then Gaozu already held Yongzhou; Sengzhen pressed hard to return west and was appointed Magistrate of Qi.
Literal must likewise render 邔 as Qi, not Zou.
The army stopped at Jiangning; Gaozu sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to take Red Nose Ford first.
The army stopped at Jiangning; Gaozu sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to take the Red Nose picket first.
赤鼻邏 uses 邏 ‘picket/patrol post,’ not a ford (津/渡).
The great host halted at Jiangning; Gaozu ordered Sengzhen and Wang Mao to lead picked troops to seize the Red Nose Ford first.
The great host halted at Jiangning; Gaozu ordered Sengzhen and Wang Mao to lead picked troops to seize the Red Nose picket first.
Literal likewise: 邏 is a picket, so ‘Ford’ invents a crossing.
